svg.title: The Multiple Arbitrage Ladder
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-multiple-arbitrage-ladder; chapter number: 2; title: The Multiple Arbitrage Ladder; subtitle: Where small-company buyers pay versus where value gets marked; chart type: horizontal_bars; unit: x earnings; bars: label: Opening Offer With Concession; min: 2.5; max: 3.0; typical: 3.0; display: Open 2.5x, concede to 3x; label: Main Street Earnings Multiple; min: 2.5; max: 4.5; typical: 4.0; display: 2.5-4.5x, screened near 4x; label: Roll-Up Add-On Purchase; min: 4.0; max: 5.0; typical: 4.5; display: Buy at 4-5x; label: Roll-Up Exit Target; min: 7.0; max: 7.5; typical: 7.25; display: Exit at 7-7.5x; label: Public Company Multiple; min: 19.0; max: 28.0; typical: 23.5; display: 19-28x; caption: Main Street businesses trade at 2.5-4.5x earnings against 19-28x for public companies, and Deibel's roll-up model buys at 4-5x to target 7-7.5x exits.; assumptions note: Typical marks the testified anchor where one exists (3x from Ruback, about 4x from the Q1 screen); where only a range was testified, typical is the arithmetic midpoint of that range, not a separate claim.; note: Attributed to Walker Deibel on Jake & Gino (xpFa8hcRy_k at 00:17:02), Walker Deibel on roll-ups (fFDPLnXTi0o) and HBS Rock Center for Entrepreneurship (oJcm3Bn-lXE at 00:57:40).

text.title: Assumptions: Typical marks the testified anchor where one exists (3x from Ruback, about 4x from the Q1 screen); where only a range was testified, typical is the arithmetic midpoint of that range, not a separate claim.

was testified, typical is the arithmetic midpoint of that range, not a separate claim.
